Expert Textiles & Handicrafts

As an expert in the Textiles & Handicrafts programme, you bring proven experience with design and production processes in textiles, or with supporting traditional craftsmanship and responsible sourcing in handicrafts. You understand how this contributes to decent work, environmental performance and the preservation of cultural heritage. Are you ready to drive change within the Textiles & Handicrafts programme worldwide and make a real impact? This is your opportunity!

About PUM

PUM is a unique NGO committed to making a positive impact on a global scale. With a network of 1,200 skilled voluntary experts, we collaborate with ambitious entrepreneurs in 26 countries and 12 programmes, sharing expertise to strengthen business ecosystems and create economic, social, and environmental value. We work closely with small and medium-sized enterprises, as well as the organisations that support them. We believe in the power of collaboration and in the magic that happens when diverse perspectives come together; Together we grow!

Who are you?

  • You have a track record of relevant experience in the textile and/or handicrafts, especially with experience in ceramic arts and design, glass crafts or decorative glasswork.

  • You are an authentic, resilient, humble and dynamic professional.

  • You appreciate cultural differences and interact with equality and respect.

  • You are eager to operate as a sparring partner in culturally diverse and changing circumstances.

  • You are hands-on and can translate knowledge into a practical plan.

  • You have excellent command of the English language, both verbally and in writing. Bonus points for French or Spanish proficiency!

  • You are comfortable with digital tools, including Microsoft Office 365.

  • Discover more about the Textiles & Handicrafts programme here.

Ready to make a difference?

As an expert at PUM, you play a key role. By sharing your knowledge and experience you’re empowering the sustainable growth of SMEs in countries worldwide. You’re not just an expert - you’re a change maker!

The role

Your application is for a place in our pool of experts for the Textiles & Handicrafts programme, not for a specific project. Once you've joined, you will be matched with up to three projects per year, either on location or remotely. Around one in three projects will be delivered as remote advice, though working solely on remote advisory projects is also possible.
On location, you’ll spend two weeks on-site with the client. PUM covers your flight and visa, while the client takes care of your accommodation, meals, and local transportation. You will also receive an expense allowance.
As PUM expert you not only share knowledge, you also:

  • Empower entrepreneurs, supporting their journey toward sustainable and inclusive business development.

  • Leave a lasting impact on the community: socially, environmentally, and economically.

  • Turn your knowledge into a hands-on project plan.

  • Expand your horizons at sector days and building a network that’s as diverse as it gets.

Eligibility and Requirements

The expert role is a voluntary position. You can apply up to and including the calendar year in which you turn 69.PUM engages experts who reside in the Netherlands, are registered in the Municipal Personal Records Database (BRP), and have Dutch basic health insurance. Prescreening (VOG) is part of the selection process. At PUM, we celebrate diversity and inclusion as essential pillars of our organisation. We embrace the uniqueness of each individual to foster an environment where everyone can thrive by being their authentic selves.

Join us!

By becoming a PUM expert, you’re not just stepping into a new role; you’re becoming a catalyst for positive change. It’s a two-way street of knowledge exchange that makes a global impact. Here’s what’s in it for you:

Continuous learning: Embrace new perspectives and gain insights by connecting with diverse people and cultures.
Professional network: Be part of a network of approximately 1,200 volunteer experts and let your network abroad grow as well.
Optimal knowledge utilization: Put your expertise to its best use, making tangible impact on businesses worldwide.
International exposure: Immerse yourself in a multicultural environment, broadening your horizons.
Building a brighter future: Contribute to the sustainable development of communities, cultivating a profound sense of fulfillment.
Stunning office moments: Enjoy regular meetups at our beautiful office in The Hague with breathtaking views.

We review applications on a rolling basis and encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as we may close the vacancy once we’ve found enough qualified candidates.

Highlights

You’ve got the skills! Why not share them? Join PUM as an expert to help build a better future for SMEs and their communities worldwide!

Bring fabrics, prints, and patterns to life on products people use every day.

We're looking for a Textile Designer to develop home and apparel products for a consumer products business that sells through Amazon and other e-commerce channels. Whether your strength is the creative side (prints, patterns, colorways) or the technical side (constructions, specs, pattern work), you'll help take textile products from concept to factory-ready files.

Location:Colombia - Fully Remote

Your Mission: Day to Day Responsibilities

  • Design prints, patterns, repeats, and colorways for home and apparel products.

  • Develop textile products across categories such as bedding, throws, towels, home décor, and apparel.

  • Create technical specifications, tech packs, and pattern work for manufacturers.

  • Define fabrics, constructions, finishes, measurements, and trims.

  • Translate trend research and product references into clear design directions.

  • Review samples and lab dips, and give feedback on color, fabric, fit, and construction.

  • Prepare and organize production-ready artwork and files.

  • Collaborate with product development, sourcing, and manufacturing partners.

  • Keep collections visually consistent and commercially relevant for e-commerce.

Your Toolbox: Skills to be Successful

  • Experience as a textile, surface, print, or technical designer in home or apparel.

  • Strong Adobe Illustrator and Photoshop skills.

  • Experience with pattern work, repeats, and colorways, or with technical patternmaking and garment or product construction.

  • Ability to create detailed tech packs and factory-ready specifications.

  • Knowledge of fabrics, fibers, weaves, knits, printing techniques, and finishes.

  • Comfortable working with physical samples, measurements, and multiple rounds of revisions.

  • Strong eye for color, trends, and what sells.

  • Experience working with overseas manufacturers is a plus.

  • Amazon or e-commerce product experience is a strong plus.

Why Adaptive Teams?
At Adaptive Teams, we don’t just fill positions – we create pathways to success. Whether you’re a seasoned pro or just starting out, we’re here to help you grow, innovate, and make an impact. If you’re looking for exciting opportunities and, a team that’s as passionate as you are, this is the place to be.

What to Expect from Our Application Process?
Once you apply, you’ll receive an email guiding you through the next steps, including an assessment tailored to the role.

After that, we’ll ask you a few brief questions about your experiences and work style—this is your opportunity to showcase what makes you unique and how you approach challenges. Be sure to check your inbox (and your spam folder, just in case) for further instructions.

We understand your time is valuable, so we strive to keep the assessments under 45 minutes whenever possible, though some roles may require a slightly longer time investment.

Once selected, you’ll have the chance to schedule an interview with our team. We aim to make the process as smooth and transparent as possible, so you’ll always know where you stand.

ABOUT QUINCE

Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.

What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.

OUR CULTURE

Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.

  • We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA. Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
  • Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
  • Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.

If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.

JOB TITLE

Leather Material Developer

Summary: At Quince, we are committed to crafting premium leather products that exemplify luxury, durability, and timeless design. We are looking for a Leather Material Developer to advance material quality, enhance supply chain consistency, and establish a strategic Leather Library to spur innovation across our product categories.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop, benchmark, and archive premium leather materials for handbags, small leather goods, belts, and accessories.
  • Establish and maintain a centralized Leather Library to ensure consistency and facilitate innovation.
  • Define and implement rigorous quality standards for leather performance, durability, and aesthetics.
  • Collaborate with QA/QC teams to address defects, color variation, and wear issues.
  • Identify and evaluate global leather suppliers ensuring traceability and ethical sourcing.
  • Manage vendor performance, negotiate terms, and drive continuous improvement in material quality.
  • Work closely with design, product development, and supply chain teams to align material innovation with brand positioning.
  • Provide technical expertise to support new product launches and premium collections.
  • Monitor supply chain risks and ensure compliance with sustainability and regulatory standards.
  • Implement traceability systems to strengthen transparency and accountability.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Textile Engineering, Material Science, Leather Technology, or a related field.
  • 8+ years of experience in leather material development, sourcing, or QA/QC within luxury or premium brands.
  • Strong knowledge of leather tanning, finishing, and testing methods.
  • Proven track record in vendor management and supply chain optimization.
  • Excellent communication and negotiation skills; ability to collaborate across global teams.
  • Passion for craftsmanship, innovation, and sustainability in leather goods.

WHY QUINCE?

​​​The Senior Manager, Assurance Integrity leads the team responsible for performance management of assurance providers in the Textile Exchange standards system to ensure credibility of the standards system. ​
